content: The International Union of Pure and Applied Physics (IUPAP) is an international non-governmental organization dedicated to advancing the field of physics. It was established in 1922, and its first General Assembly was held in Paris in 1923. The primary objectives of the Union include stimulating and promoting international collaboration in physics, sponsoring appropriate international conferences, and assisting organizing committees in their efforts. Additionally, the Union aims to support the preparation and publication of abstracts of scientific papers and tables of physical constants. It also seeks to promote international agreements on the use of symbols, units, nomenclature, and standards in physics. Furthermore, IUPAP is committed to fostering the free circulation of scientists and encouraging both research and education in the field. The Union operates under the governance of its General Assembly, which convenes every three years. Its top executive body is the Council, which oversees the activities of nineteen specialized International Commissions and three Affiliated Commissions. The Union is composed of Members who represent specific physics communities. Currently, 49 Members are affiliated with IUPAP. IUPAP is also a member of the International Council for Science (ICSU). A notable publication associated with IUPAP is the 1987 edition of Symbols, Units, Nomenclature, and Fundamental Constants in Physics, which was reprinted from Physica, Volume 146A, Numbers 1-2, page 1 (November 1987). This edition is made available online by the SP Technical Research Institute of Sweden.
